issue.title: [implementation-audit-fixes 10/23] Add doc history tables, mirrored appends, compaction checkpoints, and version selection (#216)

body:
Relay BB run pushed an update.

Pull request: #370

Tokens: 0 · Cost: $0.0000

Pushed branch `bb/relay-216-implementation-audit-fixes-10-23-add-d-thr_yg7w6yw8u2` to origin.

## Summary

Implements issue #216: retained doc-history model for the Yjs CRDT persistence layer.

- **`doc_history_updates`** table mirrors every `doc_updates` append (same id/bytes/attribution/timestamp) in the same transaction, with its own `expires_at`.
- **`doc_snapshot_history`** gained `through_update_id`, `represented_at`, and a nullable `expires_at`; **`docs`** gained `history_available_from`. New docs atomically get a non-expiring baseline checkpoint (`through_update_id = 0`) at creation.
- **Compaction** now writes a checkpoint matching the exact contract (boundary = greatest merged update's id/`created_at`, `expires_at` = represented_at + retention) in the same transaction as the snapshot write and `doc_updates` delete, and never touches `doc_history_updates` or the NULL-expiry baseline. The old periodic squash sweep (`squashDocHistory`/`runHistorySquashSweep`/`handleDocHistorySquashTask`) is removed entirely, including its cron entry and task name.
- **`openDocVersionAt`** rejects future timestamps (`ValidationError`), returns the empty doc before the first update, selects the latest applicable checkpoint and replays `doc_history_updates` forward, and returns `HistoryNotRetainedError` (HTTP 410 `history_not_retained`) before `history_available_from` or before the retention cutoff.
- **`DOC_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS`** config (default 30) validates as a positive integer; retention math uses `make_interval(hours => 24 * days)` against `transaction_timestamp()` for DST/timezone-safe boundaries.
- **`0035_doc_history_retention.sql`** adds everything additively (nullable), per expand/contract migration discipline; **`docHistoryCutoverMigration.ts`** (JS, since it merges Yjs binary updates) runs once after `runMigrations` to delete every ambiguous pre-#216 checkpoint, install one valid cutover baseline per doc, and only then tighten the new columns to NOT NULL — covered by a populated-migration test.

- `test:integration` — 78 files / 904 tests passed
- `test:e2e` — 1 file / 5 tests passed
- Workspace-wide `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `eslint .` — clean

## Summary

Addresses the code-review feedback on PR #370 (`https://github.com/dvdtrsnk/semprec/runs/102901029353`):

**Open medium findings:**
- `docPersistence.ts` — compaction checkpoint `expires_at` was anchored to the boundary update's `created_at` (content time) rather than compaction time, so a dormant doc's checkpoint could already be expired the moment it was written. Now anchored to `transaction_timestamp()`.
- `runMigrationsCli.ts` — added an addendum to the expand/contract migrations ADR (`docs/adr/2026-09-10-expand-contract-forward-only-migrations.md`) documenting when/how application-code post-migration steps like `docHistoryCutoverMigration.ts` are warranted, invoked, and guarded.

**Unmet acceptance criteria:**
1. `DOC_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS` is now validated eagerly at service startup (`serve.ts`), failing startup on an invalid value instead of only failing lazily on first doc read/write.
2. `doc_snapshot_history.through_update_id` now has `DEFAULT 0`, matching the spec.
3. The retention-cutoff boundary tests in `docs.test.ts` now pin the session timezone to UTC and derive all "now" values from a single `transaction_timestamp()` read, eliminating clock-skew nondeterminism between Node and Postgres.

While writing the ADR addendum, also closed the TOCTOU race it documents: `docHistoryCutoverMigration.ts`'s idempotency check now runs inside the transaction, after the exclusive lock is held.

Verified with the full check battery before pushing: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean, `prettier --check` clean, `test:unit` 25/25 files (177 tests), `test:integration` 81/81 files (912 tests), `test:e2e` 5/5.

## Summary

Addresses the second round of code-review feedback on PR #370 (`https://github.com/dvdtrsnk/semprec/runs/102917765071`):

**Unmet acceptance criterion #30:** Reverted the compaction checkpoint's `expires_at` back to `represented_at + make_interval(hours => ...)`, matching the issue's Task exactly. The previous round's deviation (anchoring to `transaction_timestamp()`) was unnecessary — `doc_history_updates` is mirrored and never touched by compaction, so an expired compaction checkpoint just means a query falls back to an earlier, non-expiring baseline and replays a longer stretch of the mirrored log; it never produces incorrect state or an incorrect `history_not_retained`.

**Open medium finding:** The previous round's ADR addendum rewrote the body of an already-`accepted` ADR, violating the repo's ADR convention that a file's body stays a historical record. Reverted that edit and moved the content into its own new ADR, `docs/adr/2026-09-10-app-code-post-migration-steps.md`, cross-referenced from the original's Consequences section.

**Low-priority findings:**
- Schema-qualified the `doc_snapshot_history` idempotency-guard queries (in both `docHistoryCutoverMigration.ts` and its test) with `table_schema = current_schema()`.
- The boundary tests' `SET TIME ZONE 'UTC'` was session-scoped and could leak onto a pooled connection reused by a later, unrelated test. Now scoped to a dedicated client that resets the timezone before releasing back to the pool.

Verified with the full check battery before pushing: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean, `prettier --check` clean, `test:unit` 25/25 files (177 tests), `test:integration` 81/81 files (912 tests), `test:e2e` 5/5, migration numbering script clean (36 unique ordinals).
